profile.name: Xiangli Yao
profile.introduction: Huaxu Academy's Principal Investigator, Xiangli Yao, displays exceptional expertise in various research fields despite his young age. He is a gentle yet rational soul, embracing unique insights and commitment to the research of Automata Mechanics.
profile.review:
Xiangli Yao is a 5-star Electro Gauntlets DPS who wants to fire off his Ultimate as quickly as possible to enter a higher-damage stance called Intuition, during which he can deal a larger amount of Resonance Liberation DMG.

Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts

The highlight of Xiangli Yao’s kit is his Ultimate. As explained earlier, it makes him enter the Intuition stance, which lasts a whopping 24s (needless to say it’s not going to expire on him), and he gains access to new attacks as well as a new Forte gauge during this stance. He wants to enter it as quickly as possible to start dealing the majority of his damage. 

Once his and his teammates’ buffs are ready, he enters Intuition and can start filling up his new Forte gauge, Performance Capacity, which stacks up to 5 times. He gains 5 stacks when performing a full Basic Attack chain, or when performing a full Skill chain (which leads him into a Forte Mid-air Attack ending in a plunge). Up to 3 times per Ultimate, when his Forte gauge is full, he can cast a special Forte Skill called Law of Reigns. His rotation goal, as you could’ve guessed, is to cast those 3 Forte Skills as quickly as possible before switching out. In practice, that should be performed through 2 Skill-Plunge chains and 1 full Basic chain.

Xiangli Yao also has access to another Forte gauge, called Capacity. When fully filled up through his Basic Attacks or Skills outside of his Ultimate form, he can cast a Forte Skill called Decipher which can then follow into the same Mid-air Attack as in his Ultimate form. However, this Forte gauge will not be used in practice since executing this Skill takes too much time and is overall not worth building up to.

Other than this, his passives are simple self-damage and interruption resistance increases, and his Outro launches 3 extra lightning strikes to enemies hit by other characters’ Basic Attacks.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Is Xiangli Yao a good pull? Let’s get the obvious out of the way: No. Xiangli Yao got huge team upgrades since release in the form of Lynae and Mornye being basically as ideal of supports as he could ask for, but they’re not enough. Why? A lack of raw damage numbers. Case in point with arbitrary numbers: giving a 200% boost to a character that deals 300000 damage is not as good as giving a 100% boost to a character that deals 500000 damage (you get 900000 vs 1 million). 

However, Xiangli Yao was given for free way back in 1.2. Let’s assume you’re a long-time player and you already own him on your account, whether from that or from pulling for him on a rerun in the past. Can he be okay to invest into? Sure. 

Xiangli Yao’s one of those damage dealers where you really need to set your expectations low in terms of how they can perform, however he can be okay enough to clear some of the easier endgames with. He can get passing scores with enough investment and a proper rotation. As a matter of fact, if you spend enough time optimizing his Quickswap rotations, or you own Yinlin, he can get clearing performances without necessarily taking up Lynae and Mornye, who are much better used on characters with higher base damage than him. It will be difficult in content like Endstate Matrix for example, but it is possible to get results in theory.

In conclusion, if you need a weaker team than usual to clear some of the early floors of Tower of Adversity or set another score in Endstate Matrix for example, and you already own him, Xiangli Yao could just be serviceable enough to get the job done if you choose to invest in him. Do we recommend him to any new players? That’s a definite no from a meta standpoint, but older players who already own him can still use him and get some okay-ish results out of doing so.
profile.pros:
• Fully Quickswap-friendly, huge amount of Swap Cancel windows and hence has room for a lot of rotation optimizations;

  • Can slow enemies down almost completely, making his rotation easy to perform and hard to interrupt;

  • Used to be free.
profile.cons:
• Much like the majority of the older character cast, is completely powercrept at this point. Even his own Signature isn’t best in slot for him anymore;

  • Very abnormally long rotation without Quickswap, 14s Outro buffs are very prone to expiring;

  • When he does have to dodge, his rotations get slowed down significantly most of the time;

  • Not free anymore. Good times…

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Xiangli Yao’s rotation goal is to set his own and his teammates’ buffs up before using his Ultimate to access his main damage window, and then cast his 3 Law of Reigns skills as quickly as possible before ending his rotation.

Echo Timing

Swap Cancel Nightmare: Thundering Mephis at the very end of his rotation (No Quickswap) or before his rotation starts (in Quickswap).

Void Thunder’s 5-piece bonus effect only will only be maxed out if both a Heavy Attack and a Skill are cast, so it’s important to ensure both stacks (15s duration each, separately handled) are up for Xiangli Yao’s rotation.

Standard Rotation

  • Intro 

  • Heavy Attack (Instantly interrupt via Skill)

  • Skill (Instantly interrupt via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Skill: Divergence

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Revamp

  • Skill: Law of Reigns

  • Basic: Pivot 1

  • Basic: Pivot 2

  • Basic: Pivot 3

  • Skill: Law of Reigns

  • Skill: Divergence

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Revamp

  • Skill: Law of Reigns (Interrupt when cube starts forming via Swap)

  • Echo (Swap)

  • Outro

The interruption on the last Law of Reigns allows for the first 4 hits of it to connect (most of the damage), but the last hit does not occur. Still, this saves a second over letting the full hits connect, and since Xiangli Yao’s rotation is so long to begin with, it ends up more optimal to perform his rotation this way.

Additional Tips & Tricks

Timing a Tune Break Skill with the full Forte generation of one of his Mid-air Attacks can save close to a second while sacrificing minimal damage. It is highly recommended outside of Quickswap to significantly speed up your rotations, to execute this when possible (try maximizing Tune Break Skill damage as your first priority though, considering that Xiangli Yao’s own damage is far from the highest in the game).

Xiangli Yao is a character with a lot of Quickswap freedom. The overwhelming majority of his attacks after his Ultimate are quickswappable, including his Skill (Forte and non-Forte variants), his Mid-air Attack, and his second Basic Attack. Overall, he has a lot of room to execute his rotations within your other characters’ rotations, which makes him a particularly good character to try to Quickswap with. His Quickswap rotations are very free-flow, so experiment as you wish with them!

skills.name: Probe
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 5 consecutive attacks, dealing Electro DMG.

Heavy Attack

Perform a charged attack at the cost of STA, dealing Electro DMG.

Mid-air Attack

Perform a Plunging Attack from mid-air at the cost of STA, dealing Electro DMG.

Dodge Counter

Use Basic Attack after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Electro DMG.

skills.name: Cogitation Model
skills.description:
Attack the target, dealing Electro DMG. Enter Intuition. When in Intuition:

  • Obtain 3 Hypercube(s). Each time Resonance Skill Law of Reigns is cast, consume 1 Hypercube(s). Intuition ends once all Hypercubes are consumed.

  • Basic Attack and Heavy Attack are replaced with Basic Attack Pivot - Impale, which performs up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Electro DMG.

  • Resonance Skill Deduction is replaced with Resonance Skill Divergence, which deals Electro DMG.

  • Dodge Counter is replaced with Dodge Counter Unfathomed, considered as Resonance Liberation DMG.

skills.name: Forever Seeking
skills.description:
Resonance Skill - Decipher

When Capacity reaches 100, Resonance Skill Deduction is replaced with Resonance Skill Decipher.

Consume 100 Capacity to cast Resonance Skill Decipher, dealing Electro DMG, considered as Resonance Liberation DMG.

Resonance Skill - Law of Reigns

When in Intuition triggered by Resonance Liberation and Performance Capacity reaches 5, Resonance Skill Divergence is replaced with Resonance Skill Law of Reigns.

Consume 5 Performance Capacity to cast Resonance Skill Law of Reigns, dealing Electro DMG, considered as Resonance Liberation DMG.

Mid-air Attack - Revamp

Shortly after casting Resonance Skill Decipher or Resonance Skill Divergence, use Basic Attack to perform Mid-air Attack Revamp at the cost of STA, dealing Electro DMG, considered as Resonance Liberation DMG.

Capacity

Xiangli Yao can hold up to 100 Capacity.

Every Normal Attack Probe on hit grants Capacity.

Every Resonance Skill Deduction on hit grants Capacity.

Performance Capacity

Xiangli Yao can hold up to 5 Performance Capacity.

When in Intuition triggered by Resonance Liberation:

  • Obtain 1 Performance Capacity when Stage 1 of Basic Attack Pivot - Impale hits a target.

  • Obtain 2 Performance Capacity when Stage 2 or 3 of Basic Attack Pivot - Impale hits a target.

  • Obtain 2 Performance Capacity for every Resonance Skill Divergence on hit.

  • Obtain 3 Performance Capacity for every Mid-air Attack Revamp on hit.

  • Obtain 2 Performance Capacity for every Dodge Counter Unfathomed on hit.

weapons.Comment: Iuno's Signature is Xiangli Yao's new best weapon, providing him with massive CRIT Rate and good ATK, and better stats than his own Signature like Liberation DMG DEF Ignore and Liberation DMG Bonus on the passive.
Xiangli Yao's Signature is his second best choice, granting him with solid ATK, CRIT Rate and DMG Bonus, making for an excellent stat-stick for him.
Zani's Signature weapon is generally good for Gauntlets damage dealers thanks to its consistent ATK and CRIT DMG stats as well as its easily applied DEF Ignore effect.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Xiangli Yao, who does not benefit from this weapon's Heavy Attack-oriented effects.
Strongest permanently available option and simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Xiangli Yao, who does not benefit from this weapon's Basic DMG-oriented effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Xiangli Yao, gives some extra but very negligible damage to his Echo Skill but does not benefit from any of its effects otherwise.
Another strong permanent option for Xiangli Yao that does not grant him any CRIT but instead favours ATK and Energy Regen. Inferior choice overall but still viable.

Best 4-star weapon and Battle Pass exclusive intended to function on Iuno that can still benefit Xiangli Yao by virtue of its ATK, CRIT DMG and Liberation DMG stats which increase Xiangli Yao's damage well enough to compete with low-ranked 5-star choices.
Another Battle Pass exclusive which gives CRIT Rate, a low Base ATK but some Liberation DMG Bonus increases to compensate, making for a viable 4-star overall.
Grants some extra Energy and ATK buffs with a decent Base ATK, does not compare to any 5-star choices and generally not the best, but a fine choice until stronger options are accessed.
Gives some extra ATK and DEF until Xiangli Yao gets hit after casting his Ultimate. Even under the best case scenario, this weapon isn't the best but can serve until stronger weapons are available.
Best no-gacha option for Xiangli Yao, does not give anything except some ATK. It is strongly encouraged to replace this weapon by one of the 5-star choices when possible.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Electro DMG% boost and up to an additional 30% Electro DMG% after you land a combination of 2 Heavy Attacks or Resonance Skills for a grand total of 40% additional Electro damage after fully ramped.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Offers an unconditional 12% Electro DMG and 12% Liberation DMG boost when placed in the main Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Electro focused resonators who emphasize Liberation damage and are looking to use the 5P Void Thunder set bonus.
echoes.Echo_2_Comment: Offers an unconditional 12% Electro DMG and 12% Resonance Skill DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Electro focused resonators who emphasize Resonance Skill damage and are looking to use either the 5P Empyrean Anthem Echo or 5P Void Thunder set bonus.

echoes.Comment:
Offers a 10% unconditional ATK% boost and an additional 5% ATK% for every 1.5 seconds the equipped character has been in combat - up to 20% after 6 seconds, totalling 30% additional ATK% after fully ramped. This set almost almost loses out to most characters signature elemental sets, but is generically usable across all damage characters regardless of their element.
The calculations for this set assume you're not swaping during the combo. If you will swap, the set performance drops (to 89.26%).
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Very easy echo to use that should be used at the very beginning of the burst window right after the Intro. Thanks to its instant cast there is no thinking required and you can enjoy your ATK% boost and some nice burst damage.

synergies.Comment: Easily Xiangli Yao's best partners. Lynae is the best choice by a landslide since she provides an almost equivalent buff to Yinlin's Outro with a much more impressive general buffing profile in the rest of her kit; Yilnlin is another easy to use partner, as she provides great off-field DMG via Coordinated Attacks, and amazing 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify Outro buffs. The pairings here are quite natural and effective.

Let's be clear: we don't recommend Changli+Xiangli Yao to casual players. The pair is extremely quickswap heavy and reliant on that mechanic to deal any semblance of good damage. It will underperform drastically if you don't quickswap a ton of attacks from both characters, especially compared to Yinlin. However, if you really want to push this game's limits, this duo is one of the highest damaging in the entire game. Good luck.

Good option for Xiangli Yao if you don't own the above options, as she amplifies Liberation DMG by 38% on Outro, which is a significant boost to his damage. However, Jianxin is awkward to use due to her extended field time and Energy problems. Only use her if you don't own above choices or aren't willing to quickswap.

Xiangli Yao's best option that isn't a limited 5 star if you are willing to quickswap. Xiangli Yao has several windows Yangyang can use to get a lot of attacks in and effectively allow you to play two characters at once, making for a great damaging pair. No Energy problems to worry about as well, thanks to Yangyang's Outro.

These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice generally if Lynae is in use. Shorekeeper is however a close second thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.
